kernel: the GatedDeltaNet prefill recurrence, software-pipelined blocked form (Kernel P, mx.fast.metal_kernel source string named omlx_gdn_pipelined_tb12): the exact sequential gated delta rule S = S*g; p = S.k; delta = (v - p)*beta; S = S + k*delta; y = S.q run over 12-token blocks with fp32 register state fragments
summary: omlx's default production GDN prefill for the qwen3_5 language model (Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8): a rebound gated_delta_update routes scalar-gated prefill with T >= 64 and Dk = Dv = 128 to gated_delta_pipelined. One 128-thread threadgroup owns 16 value rows and holds the fp32 state as four float4 granules per lane; the next 12-token block is prefetched into registers while the current one computes, and inside a block step t+1's operands are read before step t's cross-lane reductions. The two 128-wide dots sum in a different fp32 order than the stock per-token kernel, so the form is not bit-identical; layouts the shape predicate rejects fall back to gated_delta_blocked_seq.

models.name: Qwen3.8 GDN layers, 16 key heads and 48 value heads, Dk = Dv = 128
models.quant: any (the upstream A/B docstring does not tie the timing to a quant)
models.machine: M5 Ultra (the machine the docstring A/B names)

models.name: Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.6 series, dense and MoE (qwen3_5 language model)
models.quant: any checkpoint with q/k/v in bfloat16, float16 or float32; g, beta and state are forced fp32
models.machine: unspecified (route has no hardware probe beyond Metal availability)

settings.name: pipeline_block_tokens
settings.condition: always (constexpr TB in the generated source; the kernel name carries it as omlx_gdn_pipelined_tb12)

settings.name: value_rows_per_threadgroup
settings.condition: always (constexpr DB; one threadgroup covers 16 value rows of one v-head)

settings.name: lanes_per_value_row
settings.condition: always (rg = tid / 8 picks the row, seg = tid % 8 the lane)

settings.name: threadgroup_threads
settings.condition: always (dispatched as threadgroup=(128, 1, 1))
settings.note: _PIPE_THREADS = _PIPE_DB * 8, i.e. 16 rows x 8 lanes; the dispatch binding is gated_delta.py:930

settings.name: grid_layout
settings.value: (128 * Dv/16, Hv, B) threadgroups; the x split gives Dv/16 value-row blocks per head, so 8 x Hv threadgroups per batch at Dv = 128
settings.condition: always

settings.name: state_fragment
settings.value: fp32, 16 channels per lane held in registers as four float4 granules at columns seg + 8*i for i = 0..3 (float4 st[4]); the 8 lanes of a row cover one 128-wide state row
settings.condition: always
settings.note: the load that pins the strided layout is gated_delta.py:774; the module comment at 607-610 calls the granule placement bank-conflict-free

settings.name: state_dtype
settings.condition: always (state defaults to zeros in fp32, is cast to float32 at dispatch, and output_dtypes keeps it fp32)

settings.name: gate_input_cast
settings.value: g and beta are cast to float32 before dispatch
settings.condition: always

settings.name: input_dtypes
settings.condition: always (q, k and v must all be the same one of these)

settings.name: key_head_dim
settings.condition: always for the pipelined path (Dk == 128 in gated_delta_pipelined_supported)

settings.name: value_head_dim_multiple
settings.condition: always for the pipelined path (Dv % 16 == 0 in gated_delta_pipelined_supported)

settings.name: group_head_relation
settings.value: Hv % Hk == 0; each v-head reads the k/q rows of hk = hv / (Hv / Hk)
settings.condition: always

settings.name: y_output_dtype
settings.condition: always (output_dtypes=[in_dtype, float32])

settings.name: template_constants
settings.value: InT (input dtype), Dk, Dv, Hk and Hv are Metal template constants per shape; T is a runtime scalar input
settings.condition: always

settings.name: prefetch_depth_blocks
settings.condition: always when a next block exists (GDN_PIPE_FETCH(t0 + TB) is issued right behind the staging barrier, before the current block's steps run)

settings.name: q_reduce_group_steps
settings.condition: full blocks only (the q.S partials of steps s0..s0+3 are reduced by one xor reduce-scatter every 4 steps; the tail block falls back to a per-step reduction)
settings.note: _pipe_reduce_q4 is at gated_delta.py:651; its docstring says the result is bit-identical to reducing every step on its own (gated_delta.py:656)

settings.name: reduction_order
settings.value: both 128-wide dots accumulate as float2 partials (xy then zw fma per float4 granule) with one horizontal add each; the k.S dot is all-reduced over the 8 lanes with simd_shuffle_xor 4/2/1; y uses the same pairwise tree (per-step shuffle_down 4/2/1, or the four-step reduce-scatter)
settings.condition: always
settings.note: the module comment at 620-622 states the float2 accumulation and xor all-reduce; the per-step tree is gated_delta.py:643-646

settings.name: intra_block_pipeline
settings.value: step t+1's k/g/beta/v are read from threadgroup memory into registers at the top of step t, before step t's decay FMA and the pending q.S reductions
settings.condition: always inside a block (the nxt load at the top of _pipe_step)

settings.name: threadgroup_staging
settings.value: the current block's k and q rows in input dtype and v, g, beta in fp32 are staged in threadgroup memory (k_s[TB][Dk], q_s[TB][Dk], v_s[TB][16], g_s[TB], b_s[TB]); y is buffered per block as y_s[TB][16]
settings.condition: always

settings.name: tail_block_form
settings.value: a dynamic loop with per-step q reduction (t read as a C expression, reduce_prev=None) when the final block has fewer than 12 tokens
settings.condition: T % 12 != 0 on the last block

settings.name: y_store_width
settings.value: vec<InT,4> stores, 8 bytes per store at bf16/fp16
settings.condition: always (the per-block y_s buffer is flushed as 4-element vectors)

settings.name: route_default
settings.condition: always (module global _IMPL; the chunked and blocked_seq routes are opt-in edits)

settings.name: min_routed_tokens
settings.condition: always at the patch route (q.shape[1] >= _MIN_T)

settings.name: gating_mode
settings.condition: always (masked, vector-gated, cache-owned and state-stepped calls keep the original mlx-vlm kernel)

settings.name: fallback_kernel
settings.value: gated_delta_blocked_seq (Kernel S: 32-token blocks, 32 dv rows per threadgroup, 256 threads, Dv/32 split, per-step shuffle_down reductions, no barrier in the token loop)
settings.condition: when gated_delta_pipelined_supported rejects the layout

gates.condition: Pipelined kernel accepts: Dk == 128 and Dv % 16 == 0 and Hk > 0 and Hv % Hk == 0 and T > 0 and q/k/v all the same dtype in (bfloat16, float16, float32); otherwise gated_delta_pipelined falls back to gated_delta_blocked_seq

Patch route engages only when Metal is available and use_kernel and mask is None and T >= 64 and q.shape[-1] == 128 and v.shape[-1] == 128 and a.ndim == 3 (and no cache or state_steps argument); otherwise the original mlx-vlm gated_delta_update runs. The exact-128 gate replaced an earlier multiple-of-16/32 gate that could silently misbehave on other head dims
The engine applies the patch for the qwen3_5 GDN models unless the model setting gdn_prefill_enabled (legacy gdn_chunked_prefill_enabled) is False; default on

measured.conditions: T=8191, per layer call; the same docstring sentence reports 4.9 ms for gated_delta_blocked_seq on the same shape

lab_mapping.maps_to: our stock GDN prefill has no Dv split: encode_gdn_delta_prefill in crates/gpu/src/gdn.rs dispatches gdn_delta_step_prefill at (Hv, Dv/4) threadgroups; crates/gpu/tests/gdn_prefill_share_bench.rs exists to size exactly the share that omlx's Dv/16 staging and 8x smaller threadgroup count address
lab_mapping.note: omlx quantifies the stock form as 32x redundant k/q device traffic, about 13 GB per 16k-token layer (gated_delta.py:420), the same sentence our bench header quotes

lab_mapping.maps_to: none yet: our prefill recurrence runs one step per dispatch with no blocked staging or register-prefetch arm to sweep against
lab_mapping.note: a 12-token block with fp32 register fragments is the natural first variant if that arm is ever built

lab_mapping.maps_to: exactness discipline: upstream tests bound the pipelined form at y max abs err 2e-2 in bf16 against the stock kernel while a split prefill stays array-equal (tests/test_qwen35_gdn_prefill.py:401 and :437), so a port here would need a drifted-exactness arm, not a BitExact knob row like TURBOSPARK_GDN_LAZY_TAPE
lab_mapping.note: matches our docs: the pipelined GDN is listed among kernels that are not bit-identical to the chain they replace

notes: Everything our docs claim about this kernel checks out at this rev: 12-token blocks, 16 value rows per 128-thread threadgroup, fp32 register state, next-block register prefetch, two-level pipelining, and a different fp32 summation order for the two 128-wide dots (the module docstring says the per-step math is otherwise identical to mlx_lm's stock kernel and Kernel S, gated_delta.py:600-601). Three nuances. (1) Our doc's state fragment description, a value row with a contiguous 16-wide segment, is true of the blocked Kernel S (d0 = seg * 16, gated_delta.py:443); the pipelined kernel's lane instead holds four float4 granules strided by 8 columns (seg, seg+8, seg+16, seg+24) for bank-conflict-free staging reads. (2) The NAX-only switch our docs mention is mlx-serve's gate; omlx applies no hardware gate beyond Metal availability (qwen35_gdn_chunked.py:39), so its own default routes every qualifying prefill to this kernel on any Apple GPU, and its A/B machine M5 Ultra is a NAX part. (3) Our doc's no-barrier-in-the-token-loop claim describes Kernel S; the pipelined kernel does take one threadgroup barrier per block after staging (gated_delta.py:837) and another before the y write (gated_delta.py:845), with none inside the unrolled 12-step body. Caveats the repo records: the pipelined form is not bit-identical to the stock per-token kernel (upstream test bounds: y max abs err < 2e-2 bf16, state rel err < 1e-5, tests/test_qwen35_gdn_prefill.py:401-402), but a split prefill is array-equal to a one-shot call because every step runs the same order (tests/test_qwen35_gdn_prefill.py:437); the four-step q reduce-scatter is documented as bit-identical to the per-step reduction (gated_delta.py:656); the 3.0 vs 4.9 ms docstring A/B names no date, prompt or quant; fp32 inputs drop the blocked fallback to 16-token blocks because TB=32 exceeds Metal's 32 KiB threadgroup-memory limit (gated_delta.py:536-538), which does not affect the pipelined kernel; decode at T==1 and masked or vector-gated calls never take this route (qwen35_gdn_chunked.py:18-19).
